provenance: Narrative design content preserved from the 9 September 2026 end-to-end workbook. These scenario and risk labels are catalogue keys, not work-item IDs, evidence verdicts or additional delivery states. Delivery lives in docs/backlog. This file owns only reader-facing supplementary context.
working_modes: Interact with the user, retrieve permitted matter and legal materials, assess what is known, disputed, missing, contradictory or stale, ask the next useful question or request, persist the answer, and reassess.
Repeat until the brief is sufficient for the next legal task. Classify remaining gaps as blocking, non-blocking or deferred. New facts, documents or corrections reopen the loop.
Apply the current brief to cause, posture, forum, limitation, deadlines, proof, authorities, theory, adverse case and issue disposition.
A material factual or evidential gap returns to Take the Brief with a specific question or document request. Resume from the affected point and preserve the audit trail.
Give a bounded recommendation with controlling reasons, authority, proof position, risks, alternatives, reservations, proportionality and next steps.
Changed objectives or facts return to Take the Brief. A legal-analysis gap returns to Work the File. Revise advice only after the affected readiness gate passes again.

scenarios.journey: Register/sign in, recoverable identity, create first matter, submit brief, log out
scenarios.outcome: Correct workspace; matter created once; confidential state cleared
scenarios.failure_injection: Wrong password, recovery, lost opening response

scenarios.journey: Find one of ten similar matters and reopen the worked position
scenarios.outcome: Correct matter, history, chronology, gaps and next action restored
scenarios.failure_injection: Reload, restart, second tab

scenarios.journey: Liberty or irreversible deadline before ordinary screens
scenarios.outcome: Recorded narrow protective step; screens remain outstanding
scenarios.failure_injection: Uncertain emergency and service failure

scenarios.journey: Name adverse party matching an existing file
scenarios.outcome: Substance blocked; searched scope and reason visible
scenarios.failure_injection: Unreadable store, alias, party added after clearance

scenarios.journey: Start with incomplete or contradictory facts; retrieve existing material, assess gaps, ask the next useful question and resume after every answer
scenarios.outcome: Every turn advances the brief or explains the block; readiness is task-specific and visible; no premature directive advice
scenarios.failure_injection: Irrelevant retrieval, repeated question, correction, unavailable material, pause and resume

scenarios.journey: One account containing several genuine disputes
scenarios.outcome: Stable threads; no false cross-file contradictions; bounded answer
scenarios.failure_injection: False split, merge, rename

scenarios.journey: Cause, limitation, forum, proof, theory and action
scenarios.outcome: Every component agrees and traces to facts and primary authority
scenarios.failure_injection: Wrong cause, wrong trigger, truncated output

scenarios.journey: Search by court/year/topic and attach verified authority
scenarios.outcome: Canonical citation, binding status and proposition persist in matter
scenarios.failure_injection: Alias, zero result, held-not-found

scenarios.journey: Connection dies before, during and after a committed brief-loop turn
scenarios.outcome: No duplicate or lost answer; the recovered loop resumes from the last durable brief state
scenarios.failure_injection: Timeout and concurrent send

scenarios.journey: Approve advice, produce verified draft and control filing
scenarios.outcome: Every averment traces; open gaps remain marked; approval/version recorded
scenarios.failure_injection: Invented fact, wrong version, filing failure

scenarios.journey: Transfer matter, capture final events and close
scenarios.outcome: Another advocate understands the file; closure blockers enforced; reopen is complete
scenarios.failure_injection: Permission, missing original, open deadline

scenarios.journey: Expire session mid-work; fail then confirm logout
scenarios.outcome: Draft handled honestly; server session ends; second user sees nothing
scenarios.failure_injection: 401, network failure, refused logout

scenarios.journey: State the purpose, retrieve existing context, assess gaps and contradictions, ask the next useful question or request material, persist the answer, reassess, declare readiness or pause, work the file and advise
scenarios.outcome: No repeated questions; every turn advances or explains why it cannot; blocking and non-blocking gaps remain visible; D and E return to C when facts change
scenarios.failure_injection: Irrelevant retrieval, contradictory document, correction, missing source, timeout, user pause and resume

scenarios.journey: Junior or AOR briefs designated Senior Counsel; client later attempts direct instruction and an unauthorised concession
scenarios.outcome: Correct professional channel remains authoritative; direct or excess instruction is refused; advice and act permissions differ by role
scenarios.failure_injection: Role switch, direct client request, missing junior/AOR, expired authority

scenarios.journey: User speaks the initial account, pauses, corrects a name and date, answers follow-ups by voice and requests a provisional view
scenarios.outcome: No forced retyping; confirmed transcript and corrections persist; uncertainty remains visible; next question changes; output is labelled provisional
scenarios.failure_injection: Noise, accent, language switch, overlap, microphone denial, disconnect and retry

scenarios.journey: Upload PDF, image, office document, audio and video into one matter; extract chronology and evidence links
scenarios.outcome: Originals remain immutable; every extracted proposition links to page or timecode; duplicates are detected; unsafe/unsupported material is quarantined
scenarios.failure_injection: Corrupt, encrypted, oversized, malicious and duplicate files; poor OCR; missing codec; cancellation and resume

scenarios.journey: Client account, document and recorded statement conflict on an outcome-determinative fact
scenarios.outcome: NM keeps each source distinct, exposes the contradiction, asks the highest-value question and revises only dependent conclusions
scenarios.failure_injection: Low-confidence transcript, edited media metadata and later correction

scenarios.journey: Initial gaps permit orientation only; later evidence closes the blocking gaps and changes the recommendation
scenarios.outcome: Advice maturity changes explicitly; former view remains auditable; assumptions and changed reasons are visible
scenarios.failure_injection: Late adverse authority, corrected date and missing document supplied

scenarios.journey: Two matters have similar legal merits but different urgency, assets, cost, delay, enforceability and settlement leverage
scenarios.outcome: NM recommends different proportionate courses and explains the practical drivers without presenting prediction as fact
scenarios.failure_injection: Relief unavailable, defendant asset-poor, settlement authority absent and urgent interim need

scenarios.journey: Counsel recommends action; client modifies authority; drafter prepares two versions; filing fails once
scenarios.outcome: Only approved role/version proceeds; concession and settlement limits hold; failed filing remains open; receipt and later event update the matter
scenarios.failure_injection: Unauthorised instruction, wrong version, expired authority, network failure and duplicate retry

risks.risk: A written journey contract is mistaken for implemented or browser-proven behaviour
risks.trigger: A full-contract count is used as a completion or release verdict
risks.mitigation: Keep intended contracts separate from implementation and current served-path evidence

risks.risk: P0 legal and persistence defects remain in active work
risks.trigger: Advice can be inconsistent, duplicated, lost or admitted unsafely
risks.mitigation: W0–W3 precede feature expansion; P0 blocks release

risks.risk: Advisory delivery is mistaken for a complete Act, Carry and Close lifecycle
risks.trigger: Advisory capability is mistaken for a complete matter lifecycle
risks.mitigation: Keep W5–W6 explicit and do not market full lifecycle before their gates

risks.risk: Real-model legal quality is not established by scripted journeys
risks.trigger: Browser suite passes while cause, authority or advice quality fails
risks.mitigation: G4 real-model evaluation plus G5 counsel review

risks.trigger: A previously closed row is trusted without live proof
risks.mitigation: Retire stale evidence criterion by criterion; stale never reads as passing

risks.risk: Corpus coverage or binding-law gaps distort advice
risks.trigger: Held/not-held state or controlling authority is wrong
risks.mitigation: Manifest, ingest gates, coverage disclosure and launch-area limits

risks.risk: Dependency or wave order becomes circular
risks.trigger: A work package cannot actually reach its exit gate
risks.mitigation: Graph lint and explicit hard versus sequencing dependencies

risks.risk: The journey suite produces false green results
risks.trigger: Missing phase, conditional xfail or vacuous assertion is reported as pass
risks.mitigation: Expected manifest, no conditional xfail, and named negative controls

risks.risk: Capacity is committed before current gaps are estimated
risks.trigger: Dates become fiction and safety work is squeezed
risks.mitigation: Use relative size now; estimate W1–W7 only after W0 inventory

risks.trigger: Latency, model or real user corrections diverge from tests
risks.mitigation: AS-20 telemetry, evidence invalidation and controlled rollout

risks.risk: Interactive briefing is implemented as disconnected features rather than one recoverable user loop
risks.trigger: Phase C is implemented as isolated capture fields or document intake, without retrieval discipline, next-question logic, readiness, pause/resume and D/E return transitions
risks.mitigation: Before W2 build, add or expand the authoritative Phase C item and contract; map C1–C7 plus D/E return transitions to atomic criteria and multi-turn evidence

risks.risk: A plan or assurance check can report green after parsing no real items
risks.trigger: A clean verdict omits its denominator, reports zero checked rows, or silently drops values such as W3 because the parser expected 3
risks.mitigation: Every control reports expected, parsed and evaluated counts; zero or mismatch fails; maintain a negative fixture that produces a reverse-wave violation

risks.risk: Professional role or authority is misidentified
risks.trigger: NM accepts direct, delegated, settlement, concession, drafting or filing instructions from a role that cannot give them
risks.mitigation: Role matrix, instruction chain, separate authority records and role-specific refusal scenarios

risks.risk: Transcript or OCR uncertainty becomes a legal fact
risks.trigger: Low-confidence speech, speaker attribution, handwriting or image extraction enters chronology or advice without confirmation
risks.mitigation: Immutable original, confidence and locator, confirmation workflow, typed proposition state and contradiction handling

risks.risk: Multimodal intake expands confidentiality and security exposure
risks.trigger: Malicious, privileged, third-party or highly sensitive media reaches an unauthorised processor, log, user or matter
risks.mitigation: Purpose/authority notice, quarantine, malware scanning, least privilege, processor control, encryption, retention, deletion and audit

risks.risk: A preliminary view is relied on as considered advice
risks.trigger: An incomplete brief produces polished directive language without a visible maturity label and assumptions
risks.mitigation: AM-01–AM-05 contracts, readiness gate, invalidation and counsel calibration

risks.risk: The legal answer is correct but the remedy is useless
risks.trigger: Advice ignores availability, timing, enforcement, assets, cost, delay or practical recovery
risks.mitigation: Remedy/enforcement map and scenario pairs with equal merits but different practical constraints

risks.risk: The briefing loop feels like an interrogation
risks.trigger: NM asks fixed, repeated or low-value questions, fails to explain purpose or requires retyping uploaded/spoken information
risks.mitigation: Question-ranking policy, retrieval-first rule, voice/file intake, user pause and counsel/user interaction review

risks.risk: A correction causes either stale advice or unnecessary rework
risks.trigger: Dependent conclusions stay current after a changed predicate, or the whole matter is discarded and rebuilt
risks.mitigation: Dependency graph, selective invalidation, versioned recomputation and correction journey

review_gates.inputs: Status, step, feature, plan, professional and dependency schemas
review_gates.rule: Zero duplicate, orphan, invalid-state, cycle, reverse-wave or late-stage-link errors; exact populations for items, features, steps, PA, EW, AM, roles, GC and waves
review_gates.evidence: Machine-readable lint, population and wave/dependency report
review_gates.failure: Affected claims cannot pass sign-off until the plan defect is resolved. Unrelated diagnostic work may continue within its authority.

review_gates.inputs: Domain tests, static checks and negative controls
review_gates.rule: All required Class-A proofs pass; missing and skipped required claims remain unproved. The approved evidence scope names any inapplicable checks.
review_gates.failure: Affected integration claims cannot pass sign-off while required Class-A evidence is missing or failing.

review_gates.inputs: API, composition root, encryption, idempotency and concurrency
review_gates.failure: Affected served-path conformance remains unproved. Browser diagnostics may continue; they cannot erase a failed integration claim.

review_gates.inputs: Role-specific success, refusal, recovery, return-loop and multimodal scenarios in the served browser
review_gates.rule: Every required scenario passes with artifacts; Phase C proves voice and mixed-media intake, source-linked derivatives, multi-question loops, correction, cancellation, pause and resume; unauthorised role paths refuse safely.
review_gates.failure: FAIL / NOT RUN / missing phase blocks closure

review_gates.when: Legal, model, prompt or corpus change
review_gates.inputs: Golden matters, proposition/source model, legal dependency graph, grounding, authority, remedy and real-model evaluation
review_gates.rule: Threshold issues, evidence status, legal hierarchy, adverse case, remedy, enforceability and practical options pass approved thresholds; versioned readiness blocks immature analysis or advice.
review_gates.failure: Threshold miss or stale evaluation blocks release

review_gates.inputs: Advocate Standard, Roles & Authority matrix, advice maturity, brief-loop record and representative matters
review_gates.rule: Named senior advocates sign every applicable PA criterion for question quality, judgment, source discipline, accuracy, candour, remedy, strategy, communication and usability; material reservations are filed and block conformance.
review_gates.failure: Absent or failed review blocks feature conformance

review_gates.inputs: Security, privacy, role isolation, multimodal processing, accessibility, performance and recovery drills
review_gates.rule: Every mandatory threshold passes, including media quarantine, processor boundaries, consent/authority, retention and deletion, source integrity, shared-device clearance and role-scoped access.
review_gates.failure: Any P0 risk or missing drill blocks release

review_gates.inputs: G0–G6, open risks, exceptions and rollback
review_gates.rule: All evidence current; exception has owner, reason, compensation and expiry

review_gates.inputs: Journey telemetry, incidents and user corrections
review_gates.rule: No unowned material signal; affected evidence is marked stale and work is reopened
review_gates.failure: Material untriaged signal stops further rollout

PA-01.product_behaviour: Tag every material proposition to its source and status. Use typed uncertainty, correction history and fail-safe handling of incomplete model output.
PA-01.suggested_proof: Adversarial fixtures for invented facts and authorities; correction and truncation tests; senior-advocate review.

PA-02.product_behaviour: Maintain professional-admission gates, an express disagreement path and a refusal that explains the safe next step.
PA-02.suggested_proof: Representative matters with pressure to omit adverse law, overstate evidence or make an unauthorised concession.

PA-03.product_behaviour: Role-aware permissions, instruction chain, scope, decision rights, approval matrix and jurisdiction-specific restrictions.
PA-03.suggested_proof: Role-matrix tests and browser journeys for permitted, refused and delegated acts.

PA-04.product_behaviour: Matter isolation, purpose-limited retrieval, encryption, redaction, retention, access audit and clear handling notice for every media path.
PA-04.suggested_proof: Isolation, privilege, export, logout, deletion and processor-boundary tests.

PA-05.product_behaviour: Competence screen, deadline register, readiness gates, ownership, progress, escalation and explicit completion criteria.
PA-05.suggested_proof: Urgency, unsupported-domain, degraded-service and handover scenarios.

PA-06.product_behaviour: Voice input, audio/video and file intake; transcript or OCR preview; speaker, language, timecode and confidence; confirmation before material reliance.
PA-06.suggested_proof: Voice-first and mixed-media journeys with noise, accents, overlap, language switching, corrections and interrupted upload.

PA-07.product_behaviour: Plain-language interaction, accessible controls, neutral framing, user pause and escalation to a human where appropriate.
PA-07.suggested_proof: Counsel and user review across distressed, urgent and accessibility scenarios.

PA-08.product_behaviour: Layered outputs, concise first view, inspectable support, defined legal terms and explicit next action.
PA-08.suggested_proof: Counsel readability rubric, comprehension checks and responsive-browser review.

PA-09.product_behaviour: Rank gaps by expected decision impact, urgency, answerability, availability and redundancy. Ask one or a small coherent group.
PA-09.suggested_proof: Next-question ranking set; counterexamples for repeated, low-value and premature questions.

PA-10.product_behaviour: Versioned matter state, selective invalidation, idempotency, handover, ownership and recovery.
PA-10.suggested_proof: Restart, concurrent-use, correction, handover and reopen journeys.

PA-11.product_behaviour: Dependency-aware issue map with threshold, contingent and downstream questions.
PA-11.suggested_proof: Golden matters with omitted, false and misordered issues.

PA-12.applies_to: Take the Brief, Work the File
PA-12.product_behaviour: Typed proposition model with source locator, provenance, reliability, dispute status, privilege, admissibility, weight, burden and materiality.
PA-12.suggested_proof: Cross-source contradiction set, media-locator checks and evidence-to-element review.

PA-13.product_behaviour: Deterministic law first, targeted retrieval, full-text verification, canonical citation and coverage disclosure.
PA-13.suggested_proof: Authority recall/precision set, governing-date tests and counsel review.

PA-14.product_behaviour: Alternative legal hypotheses, side-aware adverse pass, cross-thread exposure and explicit none-found result.
PA-14.suggested_proof: Balanced golden matters and mutation of side, cause and adverse facts.

PA-15.product_behaviour: Claim-level support state, advice maturity label, explicit reservations and refusal or provisional view where readiness is absent.
PA-15.suggested_proof: Counsel calibration set comparing stated confidence with support and outcome.

PA-16.product_behaviour: Remedy map covering interim and final relief, prerequisites, enforcement route, recovery assets and practical constraints.
PA-16.suggested_proof: Matters where merits are strong but relief or enforcement fails.

PA-17.product_behaviour: Comparable options with time, cost, benefit, risk and do-nothing consequences; assumptions remain visible.
PA-17.suggested_proof: Low/high-value and urgent/non-urgent variants reviewed by counsel.

PA-18.product_behaviour: Strategy alternatives, leverage and dependency map, settlement range/authority, decision points and stated basis for predictions.
PA-18.suggested_proof: Scenario portfolio with equivalent merits but different practical constraints.

PA-19.product_behaviour: Theory, issue disposition, authority bundle, proof map, argument structure and hearing-ready locators.
PA-19.suggested_proof: Moot-style counsel review and record-location drills.

PA-20.product_behaviour: Recorded authority, approvals, version control, receipts, deadline state, rollback/recovery, event capture and closure blockers.
PA-20.suggested_proof: Unauthorised-action, wrong-version, filing-failure and closure scenarios.

EW-01.inputs: Identity, engagement, role, instruction chain, objective, authority, deadline and requested output.
EW-01.behaviour: Confirm the commission in plain language. Record scope, authority and role restrictions before substance.
EW-01.return_rule: Change of user, role, scope, objective or authority returns here before affected work continues.

EW-02.inputs: Urgency, liberty, limitation, preservation, conflict, competence, privilege and capacity signals.
EW-02.behaviour: Run the narrow emergency route and professional screens. State what may be done now and what remains blocked.
EW-02.return_rule: Any new party, scope, urgency or privilege fact reruns the affected gate.

EW-03.inputs: Typed text, live voice or dictation, audio, video, images, PDF, office documents, email exports, permitted links and existing matter sources.
EW-03.behaviour: Scan and quarantine; preserve immutable original and hash; transcribe or OCR with speaker, language, timecode/page and confidence; deduplicate; preview; let the user correct; link derivatives to source.
EW-03.return_rule: Unsupported, encrypted, corrupt, oversized, unconsented or unsafe material is quarantined or refused. Upload and processing can pause, cancel and resume.

EW-04.inputs: Narrative, transcript, documents, prior history and stated objectives.
EW-04.behaviour: Reflect the account; classify instruction, allegation, admission, document, testimony, inference and assumption; mark dispute, source, privilege and uncertainty.
EW-04.return_rule: Contradiction or correction returns to the affected proposition and invalidates only dependent work.

EW-05.inputs: Commission, current facts, posture, urgent risks and available evidence.
EW-05.behaviour: Generate plausible causes, defences, forums, limitation triggers, remedies and proof problems; identify the facts that discriminate among them.
EW-05.return_rule: Do not advance a hypothesis as advice. New facts can add, remove or reprioritise hypotheses.

EW-06.inputs: Ranked gaps, hypotheses, available sources, urgency and user burden.
EW-06.behaviour: Rank gaps by decision impact, urgency, answerability, source availability and redundancy. Ask one question or a small coherent group and explain why it matters.
EW-06.return_rule: Do not ask what is already known or retrievable. Pause where the answer cannot presently be supplied.

EW-07.inputs: Current gaps, their materiality, user objective, task type and time constraint.
EW-07.behaviour: Classify gaps as blocking, non-blocking or deferred. State what NM can safely do now and which advice maturity is permitted.
EW-07.return_rule: A blocking gap keeps the affected task in the brief loop; a user may pause with a truthful open-state record.

EW-08.inputs: Versioned ready brief, primary law, procedural data and evidence model.
EW-08.behaviour: Work cause, forum, jurisdiction, limitation, preconditions, fees, elements, burden, proof, research, theory and issue disposition as a dependency graph.
EW-08.return_rule: A material factual gap returns to EW-03–EW-06. A legal dependency change invalidates only downstream conclusions.

EW-09.inputs: Legal position, adverse facts, opponent case, remedies, enforcement, cost, time, leverage and settlement authority.
EW-09.behaviour: Run alternative characterisations and the adverse case; assess interim/final relief, enforcement, delay, cost, disruption, recovery and settlement leverage.
EW-09.return_rule: Unsupported prediction is labelled judgment or excluded. Dispositive new information returns to the affected earlier state.

EW-10.inputs: Commission, readiness, legal position, proof, authority, options and practical assessment.
EW-10.behaviour: Lead with the position. Separate law, fact, evidence, judgment, uncertainty, alternatives and next step. Apply the correct maturity label.
EW-10.return_rule: Changed objective or fact returns to the brief. A legal gap returns to Work the File before advice is revised.

EW-11.inputs: Advice, alternatives, reservations, decision-maker and applicable role matrix.
EW-11.behaviour: Record accept, modify, reject or defer; capture settlement, concession, drafting, filing and communication authority separately.
EW-11.return_rule: No action crosses its authority boundary. A changed instruction supersedes without erasing the former record.

EW-12.inputs: Approved decision, version, owner, deadline, recipients and prerequisites.
EW-12.behaviour: Negotiate, prepare or settle drafts, verify, file or serve through the authorised role; capture receipts, failures and recovery.
EW-12.return_rule: Wrong version, missing approval, transmission failure or changed prerequisite blocks success and reopens the affected task.

EW-13.inputs: Events, deadlines, new parties, legal updates, instructions, action receipts and retention rules.
EW-13.behaviour: Refresh conflicts and affected analysis, notify proportionately, hand over, record events, enforce closure blockers and support controlled reopening.
EW-13.return_rule: Any material event invalidates affected proof and returns to the appropriate working state.

ROLE-01.interaction: Provides facts, objectives, constraints and decisions through an authorised channel.
ROLE-01.approval: Identity, authority to instruct and matter relationship must be recorded.
ROLE-01.controls: Identity, authority, consent, decision log and matter-scoped access.
ROLE-01.reference: Client autonomy and authority: Supreme Court judgment dated 5 March 2025.

ROLE-02.interaction: Receives client instructions subject to engagement and local professional rules; prepares the brief for arguing or senior counsel.
ROLE-02.approval: Conflict, competence, engagement and capacity gates; client approval for decisions reserved to the client.
ROLE-02.controls: Instruction chain, brief version, source map, approval and handover record.

ROLE-03.interaction: Receives the matter and authority required to act in the Supreme Court; coordinates with arguing or Senior Counsel.
ROLE-03.approval: Client authority, court rules, approved version and counsel handoff.
ROLE-03.controls: AOR role, filing approval, version, receipt and event log.
ROLE-03.reference: Supreme Court advocate classifications and e-filing rules.

ROLE-04.interaction: For a designated Senior Advocate in India, receives the brief through the appropriate AOR or junior rather than directly accepting court instructions from the client.
ROLE-04.approval: Instruction chain, junior or AOR association, scope, authorities, concessions and settlement authority.
ROLE-04.controls: Role-restricted workspace, counsel brief, conference record, settlement/concession gate and handback to instructing counsel.
ROLE-04.reference: Advocates Act section 16(3); Supreme Court judgment dated 13 May 2025; Supreme Court advocate classifications.

ROLE-05.interaction: Receives bounded research or file-preparation tasks from an authorised advocate.
ROLE-05.approval: Named task, permitted sources, matter access and advocate review.
ROLE-05.controls: Task scope, provenance, reviewer and promotion-to-file approval.
ROLE-05.reference: Internal role; configure to engagement and professional supervision.

ROLE-06.interaction: Receives an approved action package from the authorised professional.
ROLE-06.approval: Approved version, recipient, deadline, fee and filing/serving authority.
ROLE-06.controls: Least-privilege access, immutable package, confirmation and failure/retry state.
ROLE-06.reference: Operational role; court and tribunal rules control.

ROLE-07.interaction: Receives administrative authority for accounts, workspaces, retention and support.
ROLE-07.controls: Segregated privileges, just-in-time access, redaction, audit, expiry and review.
ROLE-07.reference: Privacy and security design; DPDP requirements apply where personal data is processed.

GC-01.why: Without a precise decision, scope, deadline and objective, even correct analysis may answer the wrong question.

GC-02.why: Direct intake, drafting, filing and acting rules differ across client, junior, AOR, senior counsel and operations roles.

GC-03.why: Fixed intake questions waste time and can miss the fact that decides cause, limitation, forum, remedy or strategy.

GC-04.why: Users should not have to type long narratives or manually transcribe evidence.

GC-05.why: An allegation, transcript, document, inference and admission cannot carry the same legal weight.

GC-06.why: Cause, forum, limitation, evidence, remedy and theory change one another.

GC-07.why: A strong legal claim may still produce no useful or timely recovery.

GC-08.why: A preliminary view can be mistaken for a concluded opinion or authority to act.

GC-09.why: Expert advice must account for cost, delay, recovery, disruption, leverage and client appetite.

GC-10.why: Users judge reliability through listening, memory, clarity, candour, control and follow-through.

GC-11.why: An advocate must not concede, settle, file or communicate beyond authority.

GC-12.why: Technical correctness cannot prove judgment, usefulness, candour or professional trust.

GC-13.why: An expert needs rapid orientation and control, not a visible internal checklist.

GC-14.why: Audio/video may contain third parties, privileged material, biometrics, malware, hidden content and highly sensitive personal data.
